transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doc, it's... it's hard to talk about. What brings me in is that after I do it—after I eat like that—I just sit there looking at all the empty containers, the wrappers, and I feel so disgusted with myself. I feel like I'm not the steady, in-control man I've always tried to be. You know, out on the road, driving the rig, you have to be in control. I've been driving trucks for almost thirty years now. Started right after I got my associate's degree, which my mother always said was a waste of time since I ended up driving anyway. She always wanted me to be an accountant or something where I wore a tie. But I like the road. You see a lot of the country that way. Last week I was coming through Montana, and the sky was just incredible... but yeah, I just... I hate how I feel after I eat. It's just awful.
After you've eaten a large amount in a short period of time, do you ever try to compensate for it—like by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, no, I don't do anything like that. Making myself sick? I never could stomach the thought of it. And laxatives... man, you definitely don't want to be messing with those when you're driving an 18-wheeler. I tell you what, finding a clean restroom out on I-80 is hard enough on a good day. 

Last month, I was stuck in this massive snowstorm right outside of Cheyenne—traffic was backed up for miles, just a complete parking lot. I sat there for six hours just listening to the satellite radio. They have this classic rock station I usually like, but they play the same Eagles songs way too much. I mean, I like "Hotel California" as much as the next guy, but you hear it three times in one shift and it gets old, you know? I actually called in to the station once to complain, but you just get an automated machine. 

So yeah, taking a pill like that out on the road is just asking for a disaster. And exercise? I'm sitting behind a wheel eleven hours a day. I used to try walking laps around the truck stops, but my knees aren't what they used to be since I slipped on some black ice back in '14. They patched me up at this little clinic in Fargo, but it always aches when it rains now. 

So... no. I don't do any of those things. I just sit there and deal with the guilt.
When you're eating like that, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating once you start?

Yeah, that's... that's exactly it. Once I start, it feels like the same discipline I have out on the road just completely shuts off. I'll be sitting there, literally telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down,' but my hand just keeps going back for more. It's like I'm watching someone else do it. 

Which is crazy, because when I'm driving, I'm laser-focused. You have to be. You get these four-wheelers zipping in and out of your blind spots—especially around Chicago. Man, the Dan Ryan Expressway is an absolute nightmare. I had this one guy in a silver Honda Civic cut me off so close last Tuesday I swear I could see the brand of his sunglasses in my mirror. If I hadn't been paying attention and hit the brakes... well, 80,000 pounds doesn't stop on a dime. I had a buddy, Carl, who rear-ended a guy in similar traffic back in '08. Lost his CDL for a year and had to work at a hardware store. He hated it. Said the smell of fertilizer gave him headaches. 

But yeah, when it comes to the food... I just can't stop once I get going.
How often do you find yourself eating a significantly larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period of time and under similar circumstances?

Well, it's... it's happening a lot lately. Probably four or five nights a week. Like, some evenings I’ll heat up what I swear is just one bowl of pozole. My sister-in-law makes it, and she uses this specific kind of hominy she gets from a little market down in El Paso. 

I used to run a route through El Paso back in the late 90s. The heat down there in July, I'm telling you, it would melt the tread right off your tires if you weren't careful. I remember this one time my rig's AC went out right outside Las Cruces, and I had to drive with the windows down for three days straight. The dust gets absolutely everywhere—in your hair, your teeth... you'd be blowing brown dirt out of your nose for a week, and the noise from the highway wind just gives you a splitting headache. I finally got it fixed at this shady little shop in Albuquerque, and the mechanic charged me an arm and a leg. He had this old basset hound that just slept under my front bumper the whole time he was working... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the dinner. Yeah, so I'll start with that one bowl, and before I know it I’ve gone through the pot, a couple tamales, chips, and whatever leftovers are sitting there like I’m feeding a whole crew instead of just myself.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah, it... it really does. It bothers me a lot. I feel so ashamed about the whole thing. It's gotten to the point where I've actually started avoiding check-in calls from the younger drivers I'm supposed to be mentoring. I just... I don't want them hearing it in my voice, you know? Hearing how far off my routine I've gotten. 

I was supposed to call this kid, Tommy, last night. Good kid, just got his CDL a few months back. He's from somewhere up in Wisconsin—Green Bay, I think? Or maybe Appleton. Anyway, he's a huge Packers fan. Has this ridiculous green and gold steering wheel cover. I keep telling him that thing's gonna slip one day when he's trying to make a tight turn in a loading dock, but he won't listen. Young guys never do. I remember when I was his age, I bought this custom chrome shifter knob shaped like a skull. Thought I was the coolest guy on the interstate. Until it got so hot sitting in the sun down in Phoenix that I practically burned my palm off trying to shift into third gear. Had to wrap a fast-food napkin around it just to get out of the truck stop. 

But yeah, I just... I ignore their calls now. I sit there, looking at the phone ring, feeling terrible about myself and what I just ate.
Have you been having these kinds of eating episodes at least once a week, on average, for the past three months?

Yeah, definitely. Since I've been home with this back injury, it's been happening several nights most weeks. I really can't think of a single week in these past three months where I didn't have at least one of those episodes. 

It's this lower lumbar thing, you know? L4 and L5. The doc said it's from all the years of sitting in that cab, feeling every pothole from here to Seattle. Honestly, the seats in those newer Freightliners are supposed to be ergonomic, but they feel like sitting on a cinderblock after hour eight. I tried getting one of those beaded seat covers—you know, the ones cab drivers used to use in the 80s? My uncle had one in his old Ford LTD. That car was a boat. It was this ugly mustard yellow color, and the vinyl seats would stick to your legs in the summer. We drove it all the way to Mount Rushmore back in '76 for the Bicentennial. My brother threw up in the back seat right outside Rapid City because he ate too many of those little powdered donuts from a gas station. My dad was so mad he made him clean it up with paper towels from a rest stop...

But, uh, yeah. To answer your question, it's been every single week for the last three months, at least once a week, usually more.
Have you ever felt that your binge eating is out of your control or noticed that it happens even when you're not trying to compensate for it later?

Yeah, that's exactly it. It's like I have zero control. Once I start eating, it feels like the same discipline I had on the road just completely shuts off. Even while I’m sitting there, literally telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down,' my hand just keeps going back for more. It's like my brain and my hand aren't connected anymore. 

Which is crazy, because out on the road, you have to have so much discipline. You're managing your hours, your fuel, your weight stations... I remember this one weigh station just outside of Denver. They had this inspector, this older guy with a thick gray mustache—looked exactly like Sam Elliott. He was notorious for going over your logbook with a fine-tooth comb. One time, he held me up for two hours because he thought my tread depth on the rear passenger side tandem was a sixteenth of an inch too low. Two hours! I missed my delivery window at the distribution center and had to lay over in this dingy motel near the interstate. The motel had this vending machine in the hallway that only took exact change, and all it had were those stale cheese crackers and some off-brand cola. I remember trying to get a soda, and the machine just ate my quarters. I pounded on the glass, and the night manager came out—this kid who looked like he was about twelve—and told me if I didn't stop, he'd call the cops. 

But yeah, I don't try to make up for it later or anything. I just... I just can't stop once I start, no matter how hard I tell myself to quit.

Have you ever gone through periods where you feel you're eating a lot more than most people would in a similar time and under similar circumstances, and you feel you can't stop once you start, even if you're not doing anything like vomiting or using laxatives afterward?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, it's... it's way more than a normal person would eat, for sure. Like, some evenings I'll heat up what I swear is just gonna be one bowl of pozole. Just one bowl, right? But before I know it, I've gone through the whole pot, plus a couple of tamales, a whole bag of chips, and whatever other leftovers are just sitting there in the fridge. It's like I'm feeding a whole road crew instead of just myself. 

Speaking of road crews, man, you ever see those guys out patching the asphalt on I-10 in the middle of July? I don't know how they do it. The heat coming off the blacktop is enough to melt the soles right off your boots. I remember this one summer, must have been '98 or '99, I blew a tire right near the New Mexico border. Had to wait for roadside assistance for three hours. There was this road crew working about a mile up, and they actually sent one of their guys down on a golf cart with a couple bottles of water for me. Nice kid. Said his name was Hector. He was telling me about how his wife was pregnant with their first kid and he was picking up all this overtime to buy a crib. It made me think about when my daughter was born. We didn't have any money back then, so I actually built her crib myself out of some scrap pine I got from a buddy who worked at a lumber yard. Sanded it down so smooth you wouldn't believe it, stained it this nice dark cherry color... 

But, uh, yeah. To answer your question, it's a huge amount of food. Like I said, the whole pot of pozole and everything else, and I just... I can't stop it. And no, I don't do anything like throw it up or take laxatives or anything like that afterward. I just sit there feeling miserable.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for binge eating disorder (F50.2), with recurrent episodes of binge eating occurring at least once weekly for the past three months, marked distress, and absence of compensatory behaviors. Other differential diagnoses such as bulimia nervosa (F50.0) are ruled out due to lack of compensatory behaviors, and ADHD (F98.2) is not supported by the clinical presentation.
